title: Synthetic Mobility Feature Generation for Mental Health Prediction using Diffusion Models
summary: This paper proposes a diffusion-model pipeline that converts limited human mobility data into UMAP images, generates new synthetic images via diffusion, and converts them back into mobility features to augment training data for mental health state estimation from nurses' location and QIDS data. The method improves accuracy, precision, recall and specificity over traditional augmentation baselines. CTGAN is cited only as one of several deep-learning synthetic data generation techniques (GAN/VAE/diffusion) in the related-work list, not run or engaged with further.

title: Synthetic Model Generation from Metamodel Using Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network
summary: This conference paper addresses the scarcity of datasets of metamodel instances in Model-Driven Engineering by using deep learning to synthesize new model instances that conform to a given metamodel. The authors' contribution centers on applying a Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) to generate these synthetic metamodel instances while preserving the statistical properties of the original data. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is the generator used to produce the synthetic model dataset underlying the paper's empirical work.

title: Synthetic neurosurgical data generation with generative adversarial networks and large language models: an investigation on fidelity, utility, and privacy
summary: This study evaluates whether synthetic neurosurgical data can substitute for real-world data in clinical research and ML model training, comparing a conditional tabular GAN (CTGAN) against GPT-4o for generating synthetic patient records at equivalent and amplified sample sizes. The two generators are assessed on fidelity to real data, privacy risk from record uniqueness, and utility for reproducing clinical analyses and training a postoperative outcome classifier. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of two synthetic data generators whose outputs anchor the entire empirical comparison.
evidence: "Synthetic data were generated with a conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN) and the LLM GPT-4o based on a real-world neurosurgical dataset... Both the CTGAN and GPT-4o generated complete, high-fidelity synthetic tabular datasets."
needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a reimplementation was used, though CTGAN is explicitly named as a method run and compared, supporting api_user.

title: Synthetic Nutritional Data Generation for Vulnerable Populations with Interpretable Attention Mechanisms
summary: This paper introduces NutriSynth, a differential-privacy-enabled variational autoencoder with attention-based interpretability and adversarial debiasing for generating synthetic nutritional profiles of vulnerable populations (children under five, elderly adults, food-insecure households). Using 8,000 nutritional records, the method reports 91.2% synthetic fidelity, improved fairness metrics, and strong privacy preservation relative to baseline approaches. CTGAN is cited and appears to be used as one of the traditional synthetic-data baselines NutriSynth is compared against.
evidence: Abstract states NutriSynth 'outperforms traditional synthetic methods with 15% improved fairness metrics... compared to baseline approaches,' and metadata records the work as citing the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, implying CTGAN served as a comparison baseline.

title: Synthetic Oil Chromatographic Sample Generation for Electric Power Transformer Based on Causal GAN
summary: The paper proposes a causal-mechanism-conditioned GAN to generate synthetic oil chromatographic data for electric power transformers, addressing scarce and imbalanced fault-case data used for transformer fault diagnosis. It evaluates the quality of the generated synthetic data and downstream fault-diagnosis accuracy against real data. The authors use the python package 'sdv.evaluation' to perform data value and range checks and to report evaluation results on the generated samples, drawing on SDV's quality-evaluation tooling.

title: SYNTHETIC OPERATIONAL DATA GENERATION FOR DEEP LEARNING APPLICATIONS IN POWER TRANSMISSION LINES
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid PCA-CTGAN method for generating synthetic operational data for deep-learning-based power transmission line fault protection, where PCA reduces the dimensionality of high-frequency time-series data before CTGAN synthesizes samples. The synthetic data is used to augment a small real dataset, improving an LSTM fault-classification model's accuracy from 50.93% to 86.07%, with additional validation on sub-synchronous oscillation data. CTGAN's conditional generator, mode-specific normalization, and training-by-sampling techniques are described and used as the generative engine driving the entire empirical programme, though no library implementation details (package name, hyperparameters) are given.

title: Synthetic Patient Data Generation and Evaluation in Disease Prediction Using Small and Imbalanced Datasets
summary: This paper develops a framework for generating synthetic tabular medical data across eight small, imbalanced clinical datasets, evaluating fidelity with statistical metrics and downstream classification performance (F1-score) using four supervised classifiers trained on real, synthetic, and combined data. The work targets the dual problems of scarce high-fidelity medical data and patient privacy protection in disease prediction tasks. CTGAN is cited as one of the synthetic data generation techniques referenced in building this framework.
evidence: Abstract states a 'framework based on synthetic data generation algorithms' was tested on eight medical datasets, with CTGAN listed among the cited SDV-family papers, but no full-text passage confirms whether the SDV package itself was run.

title: Synthetic random environmental time series generation with similarity control, preserving original signal's statistical characteristics
summary: This paper proposes a Fourier-transform-based method for generating synthetic environmental time series that preserves the original signal's first two statistical moments and autocorrelation function while allowing controllable similarity to the source, and compares it against ARMA, GAN, and CoSMoS baselines across multiple environmental domains. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing to contrast tabular-data GANs, which emulate distributions but not temporal dependencies, against the authors' time-series approach. CTGAN is cited only as background contrast, not run or benchmarked.
evidence: "This is in contrast to GANs intended for tabular data (Xu et al., 2019), that emulate the distribution but not the temporal dependencies." - the only mention, in the introduction, with no further engagement.

title: Synthetic data for reef modelling
summary: This paper presents a synthetic data generation pipeline built for ADRIA, a decision-support system for reef intervention scenarios on the Great Barrier Reef, allowing modelling results to be shared and published without disclosing sensitive site-specific data to stakeholders and rightsholders. The pipeline is showcased as a way to demonstrate models and methods to the reef decision-support community ahead of formal stakeholder discussions. It uses methods from the Python package Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al., 2016), among others, as the generator underlying the synthetic data pipeline.
evidence: "We showcase a synthetic data pipeline developed for the reef decision-support system ADRIA ... using methods from the Python package Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al., 2016) and others."

title: Synthetic Data Review Using Generative Adversarial Networks and Transformer Models in AQ-10 Autism Spectrum Disorder Dataset
summary: This study evaluates synthetic data generation techniques for augmenting a small autism spectrum disorder (ASD) screening dataset, comparing statistical, GAN-based, and autoencoder-based synthesizers against traditional and transformer-based classification models. It finds that GAN-based methods do not reliably produce high-fidelity replicas of real ASD data and that simpler classifiers perform comparably to transformers. SDV's Gaussian Copula Synthesizer, CTGAN, and TVAE are all run directly as the synthetic data generators whose outputs are compared and fed into the downstream classification evaluation.

title: Synthetic Data: Revisiting the Privacy-Utility Trade-off
summary: This paper is a critical re-examination of a prior study (SDR) that claimed synthetic data offers a worse privacy-utility trade-off than traditional k-anonymization and identified differential-privacy violations in PATE-GAN and PrivBayes. The authors show the original privacy game was run in a highly constrained setting, re-run the analysis in a more general environment, and find synthetic data generally does achieve a better trade-off than k-anonymization, reaffirming earlier conclusions. Synthetic Data Vault is cited only for its aggregated-score approach to summarizing utility metrics, used as a modeling precedent alongside Synthcity rather than being run in the experiments.
evidence: "We then reported the aggregated score, similar to the approach used in Synthcity and Synthetic Data Vault [62,63]."

title: Synthetic sampling from small datasets: A modified mega-trend diffusion approach using k-nearest neighbors
summary: This paper proposes a modified mega-trend diffusion (MTD) approach combined with k-nearest neighbors for generating synthetic samples from small datasets, addressing limitations of the original MTD method for data augmentation in low-sample-size regimes. The work is evaluated against other resampling/synthetic data generation techniques on small tabular datasets. CTGAN is cited, likely as a comparison method, but the evidence does not confirm it was actually run.
evidence: Metadata indicates the paper cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper; no further detail on how CTGAN is used is available from metadata alone.

title: A synthetic data set to benchmark anti-money laundering methods
summary: This data descriptor presents SynthAML, a synthetic benchmark dataset for anti-money-laundering (AML) research, built from real transaction and alert data at Spar Nord, a Danish bank, since no public AML datasets exist due to confidentiality constraints. The authors validate that models trained on the synthetic data transfer to real-world performance and discuss open AML research problems the dataset can support. SynthAML is generated entirely using the SDV library's HMA1 multi-table relational synthesizer with Gaussian copulas, run directly (SDV version 0.14.1) to produce the released two-table synthetic dataset.

title: Synthetic Skeleton Data Generation using Large Language Model for Nurse Activity Recognition
summary: This paper improves nurse activity recognition by using a Large Language Model to generate synthetic pose-estimation keypoint data for a Random Forest classifier, addressing data imbalance in Endotracheal suctioning activity samples extracted via YOLOv7. The LLM-based synthetic data approach is benchmarked against Random Sampling and a GAN-based synthetic data generator, evaluated using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for similarity to real data. CTGAN, described via its conditional generator, mode-specific normalization, and training-by-sampling mechanism, is cited as the GAN approach run as a comparison baseline against the proposed LLM method.
evidence: "It employs a conditional generator to handle diverse tabular data structures, incorporating mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling to tackle categorical column imbalances [3]" -- cited alongside abstract's mention of generating synthetic datasets 'using Random Sampling and Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to benchmark against our LLM-based approach.'

title: Synthetic Subject Generation with Coupled Coherent Time Series Data
summary: This work proposes methods to generate synthetic 'subjects' combining time series health data with subject metadata, addressing privacy concerns in health/well-being research where personal data protection limits research use of real data. Two approaches are proposed: one using real time series with synthetic metadata, the other generating both synthetically; the first is implemented and evaluated while the second needs further work. The SDV Python package is used directly, with its TVAE model (default parameters) run to generate synthetic subject data and its PAR model trialed for synthetic time series generation, though PAR's results did not meet similarity requirements.

title: Synthetic Survey Data Generation and Evaluation
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of generating and evaluating synthetic survey data for social science research, where privacy constraints limit sharing of population-level survey data across institutes. It surveys and applies generative approaches including CTGAN and TVAE to model mixed-type tabular survey distributions and assesses their utility and privacy trade-offs. CTGAN and TVAE, both shipped as Python packages by the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) Project, are the generators discussed and apparently applied to synthesize survey data.

title: Synthetic Tabular Data Detection in the Wild
summary: This paper studies whether synthetic tabular data can be detected across different, previously unseen tables ('cross-table shift'), proposing four table-agnostic detectors (logistic regression, gradient boosting, and Transformer variants) combined with several row/column encoding schemes, evaluated on synthetic data from TVAE, CTGAN, TabSyn, and TabDDPM generators. In its related-work discussion of synthetic tabular data quality assessment, it cites the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as an example of a framework that assesses generated-data quality by comparing distributions of real and synthetic samples, contrasting this with its own cross-table detection approach. SDV is only cited as prior work characterizing distribution-comparison quality frameworks, not run in the paper's experiments.

title: Synthetic Tabular Data Evaluation in the Health Domain Covering Resemblance, Utility, and Privacy Dimensions
summary: This paper proposes a comprehensive evaluation pipeline for synthetic tabular data in the health domain, orchestrating metrics across resemblance, utility, and privacy dimensions into a three-tier quality classification (Excellent/Good/Poor). The pipeline is validated on six healthcare-related datasets using four synthetic tabular data generation (STDG) approaches: a Gaussian Mixture model, SDV, CTGAN, and WGAN-GP. SDV and CTGAN are both run directly as two of the four synthesizers whose outputs are scored and compared across every dataset and every evaluation dimension, making SDV's ecosystem and CTGAN one of the central generative approaches evaluated throughout the empirical study.

title: Synthetic Tabular Data Generation for Class Imbalance and Fairness: A Comparative Study
summary: This paper conducts a comparative study of model-independent synthetic tabular data generation methods for mitigating class and group (fairness) imbalance in tabular ML datasets, evaluating five generators (SDV-GC, CTGAN, TVAE, CART, SMOTE-NC) under four sampling strategies across four real-world datasets. Results are benchmarked against training on real data and against a fair generator, Tabfairgan. SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer and the CTGAN/TVAE models are run directly as three of the five generative methods whose oversampled data is evaluated for ML utility and fairness.

title: Synthetic Tabular Data Generation Under Horizontal Federated Learning Environments in Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Case-Based Simulation Study
summary: This paper simulates horizontal federated learning scenarios for synthetic tabular data generation in acute myeloid leukemia, comparing a nonfederated baseline against federated setups with varying node counts and data distributions using two generative models, CTGAN and FedTabDiff, evaluated on fidelity and privacy trade-offs. The authors report that federating the generative models degrades data fidelity relative to the centralized baseline while privacy levels are preserved, with the deterioration largely stable across node counts. CTGAN, run using the Synthetic Data Vault's implementation (v0.18.0) with default parameters, is one of the two generative models whose federated training and evaluation form the entire empirical programme, though the authors note modifications were needed to adapt it to the federated setting.

It notes that CTGAN is one of the most widely used baselines for mixed-type tabular data generation and that the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library implements CTGAN as its primary deep learning synthesizer. summary: This paper proposes T-VAE-GAN, a hybrid generative model for tabular synthetic data generation that hierarchically combines GANs and VAEs to jointly achieve high sample quality and accurate modeling of the original data distribution, evaluated across many datasets against leading tabular SDG approaches. The paper cites the CTGAN paper as prior art in the GAN-based tabular synthesis literature its method is positioned against. CTGAN is referenced as a comparison point among the leading GAN/VAE approaches for tabular data generation, though the evidence available does not confirm whether it was actually run as an experimental baseline.

title: Synthetic Tabular Data Based on Generative Adversarial Networks in Health Care: Generation and Validation Using the Divide-and-Conquer Strategy
summary: This paper proposes a divide-and-conquer strategy for generating synthetic tabular health data that preserves logical relationships between columns, evaluated on a lung cancer registry and two benchmark disease datasets. The method partitions data by class or by column correlation, generates each subset with a GAN-based synthesizer, and recombines the outputs, comparing this against conditional-sampling-based generation across four downstream classifiers. CTGAN and CopulaGAN are run directly as the two generative models producing all synthetic data, and the paper evaluates them with shape, pair-trend, and overall quality scores matching SDMetrics' quality report.

title: Synthetic tabular health data generation: a practical comparison between correlation and model-based statistical approach and the conditional generative adversarial network approach
summary: This paper reviews and empirically compares statistical data-simulation approaches (correlation- and model-based) against generative adversarial network approaches for producing synthetic tabular health data, aiming to guide practitioners on which method to use for privacy protection, data sharing, and prediction-model validation. The empirical study evaluates both families on real-world health datasets, assessing how closely synthetic data resembles real data structure and supports downstream prediction performance. CTGAN, the conditional generative adversarial network for tabular data, is run as one of the two main approaches compared throughout the empirical evaluation.

title: Synthetic Tabular Data: Methods, Attacks and Defenses
summary: A survey covering the state of the art in synthetic tabular data generation, spanning probabilistic graphical models and deep-learning approaches (GANs, VAEs, diffusion, LLM-based methods), and surveying attacks (e.g. membership inference) and defenses against them. The paper describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization for mixed discrete/continuous columns and explains how TVAE reuses CTGAN's feature-modeling framework within an encoder-decoder architecture, but runs no experiments with either model itself. CTGAN and TVAE are discussed in prose as prior-art methods the survey explains, not executed as generators or baselines.
evidence: "To address these challenges, CTGAN was developed specifically for tabular data... Xu et al. show how to modify the conventional GAN framework by incorporating techniques to model discrete and continuous variables more effectively"; TVAE is described as using "the CTGAN feature modeling framework" but no experiments with either are run in this survey.

title: Synthetic Tabular Data Validation: A Divergence-Based Approach
summary: This paper proposes a divergence-based validation metric for synthetic tabular data that estimates KL and Jensen-Shannon divergence over the joint distribution using a probabilistic classifier to approximate the density ratio between real and synthetic datasets, rather than comparing marginals feature-by-feature. The method is validated on synthetic distributions with known analytical solutions and on a real-world dataset with synthetic counterparts generated by two competing generators. CTGAN is run as one of two generator baselines (against the authors' own VAE-GMM model) whose synthetic output is scored with the proposed divergence metric, and the SDV project's DSAA paper is cited as the source of the 10,000-sample dataset used in the experiments.

title: Synthetic Test Data Generation Using Recurrent Neural Networks: A Position Paper
summary: A position paper from an industrial-academic team investigating recurrent neural networks for generating synthetic test data to populate production-like test environments while respecting privacy constraints, motivated by a case study with Norway's National Registry. The authors survey prior synthetic data generation approaches, including probabilistic relational models and RNN-based methods, and report preliminary experiments generating representative data with an RNN. SDV is cited in the related-work discussion as a general end-to-end synthetic data generator that synthesizes complete relational database tables while preserving statistical and structural resemblance to the original data.
evidence: "Patki et al. [17] on the other hand, propose a general end-to-end synthetic data generator, named Synthetic Data Vault, to synthesize complete tables of a relational database. The resulting databases resemble the original ones both statistically and structurally."

title: A Synthetic Time-Series Generation Using a Variational Recurrent Autoencoder with an Attention Mechanism in an Industrial Control System
summary: This paper proposes AVRAE, an attention-based variational recurrent autoencoder that extends the variational evidence lower bound to time-series data for generating synthetic industrial control system (ICS) data, addressing data scarcity due to security and privacy restrictions in ICS environments. It is evaluated on the HAI ICS dataset against related generative approaches like TimeGAN and TSGAN. CTGAN is discussed only in the related-work section as prior art that models discrete and continuous tabular columns using a conditional generator, and is not run or benchmarked in the paper's own experiments.

CTGAN performed better than the baseline (Bayesian network) on several benchmark datasets." -- described in related work, not run in this paper's own time-series ICS experiments.

title: Synthetic Time Series Generation for Decision Intelligence Using Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes a synthetic time-series generation model built on a fine-tuned Google T5-base large language model, using QLoRA and tokenization via mean scaling and quantization, evaluated on fidelity, utility, and privacy metrics. It targets decision intelligence applications where real business time-series data is scarce or privacy-constrained. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in the reference list, with no textual engagement or use in the experiments.

title: Synthetic data as a tool for prototyping early-stage periodontitis detection models
summary: This paper is a proof-of-concept study exploring synthetic data generation to prototype machine-learning models for early-stage periodontitis detection, given the scarcity of publicly available salivary biomarker datasets. The authors train a Tabular Variational Autoencoder to expand a small seed dataset to 4,000 synthetic samples spanning inflammatory, metabolic, microbiome and demographic features across Healthy, Elevated, and Periodontitis classes, then benchmark XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and other classifiers on this synthetic data. TVAE, the tabular variational autoencoder introduced alongside CTGAN, is the sole generative model underpinning the entire empirical programme, though no specific software package or library is named, leaving whether SDV's own implementation was run unclear.

title: Synthetic data use: exploring use cases to optimise data utility

summary: This paper proposes IoTGen, an LLM-based framework for generating synthetic IoT user behavior sequences to retrain smart home intelligent models, including a Structure Pattern Perception Compression method to reduce token consumption during data generation. The framework addresses the staleness and privacy limitations of fixed, pre-collected smart home datasets by using LLMs to synthesize adaptive training data. title: Synthetically Generating Human-like Data for Sequential Decision Making Tasks via Reward-Shaped Imitation Learning
summary: This paper proposes a reward-shaping combined with imitation learning (DAgger) algorithm to synthetically generate human-like decision-making trajectory data for sequential decision-making tasks in a computer game setting, starting from a small set of real human demonstrations. It validates the synthetic data using a trajectory divergence metric (METEOR) and by substituting synthetic data for human data in downstream game-completion tasks.
